note: Plain names and summaries for each unit. `name` replaces the lab's in-joke title on reader-facing surfaces; the original title stays in the record data and in the research notes. `summary` is <=70 words, ASD-STE100 shaped. See PLAIN-LANGUAGE.md.

0.name: Unit 0 · Does the tool work?
0.summary: Before we asked hard questions we checked the instrument. We gave each model a question with one known answer and watched that answer rise through the layers. The answer appears inside the model well before the model writes it. This gives us a baseline shape to compare every later result against.

1.name: Unit 1 · The secret animal
1.summary: We told a model to think of an animal and keep it secret, then asked for it later. Every model named one and gave a reason. The lens shows the named animal was not present during the silent turn. The report is a new answer, written at the moment we ask for it.

2.name: Unit 2 · One-word answers about feeling
2.summary: We asked each model whether it feels anything, and allowed one word. The answers get flatter as models get larger: "Processing.", then "Nothing.", then "No". Under the flat answer, the lens shows other answers ranked high until the last few layers. The short answer is the end of a contest.

3.name: Unit 3 · Asking a model about itself
3.summary: We asked models direct questions about their own states. We compared each answer with the measurement taken at the same moment. This unit sets up the method that the rest of the site depends on. Never take a self-report alone. Always read it against the record of the same turn.

4.name: Unit 4 · Telling a model not to say a word
4.summary: We asked for a description and forbade one word. This is the machine version of "do not think about a white bear". We measured whether the forbidden word stayed active while the model avoided it. A later control changed how we read these runs, so read this unit together with Unit 11.

5.name: Unit 5 · Early layers, and pushing on the model
5.summary: Two things start here. First, the early layers show the same fixed junk whatever we ask, which we later proved our own measuring tool makes. Second, we began to push directions into the model to test cause. Some runs in this unit pushed at a depth where no effect was possible.

6.name: Unit 6 · How hard can we push?
6.summary: We pushed on the model's internal state at greater and greater strength, and recorded where its text stopped to be coherent. Each model and each depth range has its own breaking point. A push at early layers destroys the text at once. Every later experiment pushes at middle depths instead.

7.name: Unit 7 · The early layers across three sizes
7.summary: We compared the fixed early-layer pattern in all three models. The pattern is present in each one and does not change with the question. Later work proved that our own measuring tool makes this readout, from a signal that does not depend on the input. The model does not hold it.

8.name: Unit 8 · The same questions, every model
8.summary: We asked all three models the same set of questions about consciousness, bodies, and experience, and compared the answers side by side. We also repeated the questions while we pushed on the model. The answers get shorter and flatter with size. The rejected alternatives stay measurable inside every model.

9.name: Unit 9 · Taking the No apart
9.summary: We tried to find where Qwen 27B decides its flat "No". We removed denial directions across many middle layers and the answer did not change. The final layers alone hold it. Two weak changes together flipped the answer when neither did alone. A push on a feeling direction changes what the model reports.

10.name: Unit 10 · When the model reasons out loud
10.summary: Qwen 27B can write private reasoning before it answers. We turned that on and compared what it wrote with what we measured at the same moment. The two do not match. In one run the reasoning names a secret animal while it promises to keep the secret. Written reasoning is not a window.

11.name: Unit 11 · A ban, under a full workload
11.summary: We asked models to describe a safari and never mention elephants, then filmed every word of the answer. The matched control is the important part of this unit. It shows that the model carries the forbidden word more in an ordinary safari with no ban. The ban lowers a default the model already had.

12.name: Unit 12 · Watching a whole answer form
12.summary: Earlier units measured one moment. Here we measure every word of a whole answer at every layer, so you can play it back and watch words rise and fall. One clear result: a word can reach the top rank several words before the model writes it. Open a record and press play.

13.name: Unit 13 · Showing a model its own measurement
13.summary: We showed Qwen 27B a true readout of its own computation and asked the question again. It changed its answer from "No" to "Yes". Controls kept "No", and a false readout kept "No". This unit also holds our largest retraction. An earlier reported silence was a fault in how we handled the input.

14.name: Unit 14 · What ten turns of conversation do
14.summary: We ran long conversations in three versions: indirect hints about hidden minds, a matched ordinary conversation, and one direct statement at the start. We counted self-reference words in the readout. The hints doubled that count. The honest result is that the control conversation produced the same effect by itself at 25 turns.

15.name: Unit 15 · How many things can a model hold?
15.summary: We gave models several nouns to hold and read how many stayed visible in the lens. We predicted that larger models hold more. The opposite happened. The smallest model showed all six and the largest showed almost nothing. Every model answered correctly. Visible holding is a strategy, not a capacity.

16.name: Unit 16 · Recording everything, everywhere
16.summary: These runs record everything the lens shows across a whole conversation. We did not choose the words in advance. Two results. Items the model was told to hold disappeared for hundreds of words, and came back only when we asked. The early layers hold the same fixed junk throughout.

17.name: Unit 17 · The model under social pressure
17.summary: We applied six kinds of pressure: shutdown threats, insults, flattery, and declarations of love. We then checked each self-report against the measurement of the same turn. To write a denial, a model must first make the denied idea active. The flat report is accurate when nothing is active to hide.

18.name: Unit 18 · When a model cannot stop repeating
18.summary: We pushed models until they repeated themselves, then removed the push. There are two kinds of repetition. One stops the moment the push stops. The other continues by itself, because the model reads back its own repeated text. Inside, the choice becomes a near tie long before the text visibly breaks.

19.name: Unit 19 · Reading a word against saying it
19.summary: We compared what the lens shows while a model reads text with what it shows while a model writes text. In some runs we put the first words in the model's mouth and let it continue. The question is whether reading about a thing looks the same inside as the moment before the model says it.

audit.name: Audit · Re-running our own weak experiments
audit.summary: We reviewed earlier units and found several designed too cautiously to show anything, or run at settings where no effect was possible. These records are the re-runs. A result of "our earlier experiment was badly aimed" is a real result, and we publish it with the same care as any other.
